stem:
Naveen checks flat card cut-outs meant as nets for a cube.

Which arrangements are valid mathematical nets for a cube? Two options are correct.

options.text: Six squares in a straight row.
A cross of five squares with one more square joined to a side of the centre strip.
Four squares in a row, with one square joined above the second and one joined below the third.
Six face squares plus thin joining flaps treated as extra faces.

teacher.key_rationale: B and C fold into a cube without face overlap. A has six faces but cannot wrap a cube. D treats support flaps as net faces, which a mathematical net excludes.
